claims.claim: The Federal Aviation Administration issued a rare nationwide ground stop on Friday afternoon after outdated air-traffic communications equipment became overloaded with data and began to fail.
claims.episode_span: outdated air-traffic communications equipment became overloaded with data and began to fail
claims.source_title: What to Know About Friday’s Nationwide Ground Stop
claims.supporting_quote: The Federal Aviation Administration issued a rare nationwide ground stop Friday afternoon, after outdated air traffic communications equipment became overloaded with data and began to fail, officials said.

claims.claim: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said radar and other air-traffic communications started to falter at 3:36 p.m. when old routers became overloaded with data, and that the failures were not universal but were pervasive enough to prompt a nationwide moratorium on takeoffs.
claims.episode_span: radar and other air-traffic communications started to falter at 3:36 p.m., when old routers became overloaded with data
claims.source_title: What to Know About Friday’s Nationwide Ground Stop
claims.supporting_quote: Sean Duffy, the transportation secretary, told reporters at the White House Friday night that the radar and other air traffic communications started to falter at 3:36 p.m. when old routers became overloaded with data.

claims.claim: More than 8,200 flights, or over 31 percent of those scheduled in the United States, were canceled, and the ground stop lasted nearly five hours, the longest nationwide ground stop since September 11, 2001.
claims.episode_span: More than 8,200 flights were canceled. That was over 31 percent of the flights scheduled in the United States.
claims.source_title: US nationwide flight ground stop: "Our routers got overloaded with data"
claims.supporting_quote: More than 8,200 flights, or over 31% of those scheduled in the United States, were canceled. The ground stop lasted nearly five hours and was the longest in the country since September 11, 2001.

claims.claim: Officials blamed outdated air-traffic communications equipment, said there was no evidence of a cyberattack, and said the airspace had reopened and flights had resumed.
claims.episode_span: Officials blamed outdated air-traffic communications equipment. France 24 said there was no evidence of a cyberattack.
claims.source_title: US nationwide flight ground stop: "Our routers got overloaded with data"
claims.supporting_quote: Officials blamed outdated air traffic communications equipment, and said that there was no evidence of a cyber attack. The airspace is now reopened and flights have resumed.

claims.claim: The outage stranded thousands of passengers, and airlines and airports were still struggling to recover.
claims.episode_span: The outage stranded thousands of passengers. It caused widespread delays.
claims.source_title: What to Know About Friday’s Nationwide Ground Stop
claims.supporting_quote: The outage stranded thousands of passengers and caused widespread delays from which airlines and airports are still struggling to recover.

claims.claim: Administration officials demanded that lawmakers approve tens of billions of dollars more to accelerate systemwide air-traffic upgrades.
claims.episode_span: Administration officials demanded that lawmakers approve tens of billions of dollars more to accelerate systemwide upgrades.
claims.source_title: What to Know About Friday’s Nationwide Ground Stop
claims.supporting_quote: It also highlighted persistent vulnerabilities in the aging U.S. air traffic infrastructure and a funding fight, as administration officials demanded lawmakers approve tens of billions of dollars more to accelerate systemwide upgrades.

claims.claim: Duffy insisted the cause was antiquated legacy equipment, not recent upgrades.
claims.episode_span: Duffy insisted that the failure was caused by the antiquated, legacy communications equipment, not by recent upgrades
claims.source_title: What to Know About Friday’s Nationwide Ground Stop
claims.supporting_quote: Mr. Duffy insisted that the failure was caused by the antiquated, legacy communications equipment, not recent upgrades to the system.

claims.claim: Markwayne Mullin said there was zero evidence of a cyberattack and suggested that new equipment and technology added to old infrastructure had overwhelmed it.
claims.episode_span: He suggested that new equipment and new technology Duffy’s department had added to the old infrastructure was what had overwhelmed it.
claims.source_title: What to Know About Friday’s Nationwide Ground Stop
claims.supporting_quote: “We’ve seen zero evidence that this was a cyberattack,” Mr. Mullin said, suggesting that new equipment and new technology the Mr. Duffy’s department had added to the old infrastructure was what had overwhelmed it.

claims.claim: Microsoft said on Saturday morning that it had completed efforts to address the underlying issue and restored service to the remaining impacted customers and regions.
claims.episode_span: the company said it had completed its efforts to address the underlying issue of the incident and restored service
claims.source_title: Microsoft says services fully restored after global outage
claims.supporting_quote: On its Microsoft 365 status page, the US-based firm said: “We have completed our efforts to address the underlying issue of the incident and restored service to the remaining impacted customers and regions.

claims.claim: The Microsoft outage affected governments, courts, healthcare services, businesses, airlines and banks, and Japan, Singapore and Australia reported effects on some operations.
claims.episode_span: Governments including those of Japan, Singapore and Australia reported that the hours-long episode had affected some of their operations.
claims.source_title: Microsoft says services fully restored after global outage
claims.supporting_quote: Governments including those of Japan, Singapore and Australia reported that the hours-long episode had affected some of their operations.

claims.claim: In the UK, hospital staff resorted to paper records and courtrooms scrambled to locate fax machines during the Microsoft outage.
claims.episode_span: hospital staff resorted to paper records and courtrooms scrambled to locate fax machines
claims.source_title: Microsoft says services fully restored after global outage
claims.supporting_quote: In the UK vital public services were hit, with hospital staff resorting to paper records and courtrooms scrambling to locate fax machines.

claims.claim: Downdetector received Microsoft outage reports from more than 70 countries and territories, and from 74 countries and territories within an hour.
claims.episode_span: it received reports from 74 countries and territories within an hour after problems first emerged
claims.source_title: Microsoft says services fully restored after global outage
claims.supporting_quote: After problems first emerged Downdetector said it received outage reports from 74 countries and territories within an hour .

claims.claim: Microsoft said more than 430 million people use Microsoft 365 apps, and said in January it had more than 450 million paid commercial 365 subscriptions.
claims.episode_span: more than 430 million people use Microsoft 365 apps
claims.source_title: Microsoft says services fully restored after global outage
claims.supporting_quote: More than 430 million people use Microsoft 365 apps, Microsoft said on its website.

claims.claim: Problems started about midday Thursday in the US and 6pm in the UK; Microsoft apologised Friday and said the outage was not related to cyber or AI agents and was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced after a recent network change.
claims.episode_span: Problems started appearing at about midday on Thursday in the United States and 6 p.m. in the United Kingdom.
claims.source_title: Microsoft says services fully restored after global outage
claims.supporting_quote: It said the incident “was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced” after a recent network change.

claims.claim: Tim Clement-Jones called the outages an I told you so moment on Britain’s dependence on US tech, and Jeremy Singer said the problem emphasised dependence on one company’s digital infrastructure.
claims.episode_span: called the widespread outages of vital government services an “I told you so moment”
claims.source_title: Microsoft says services fully restored after global outage
claims.supporting_quote: Tim Clement-Jones, a former chair of the House of Lords artificial intelligence select committee, said the widespread outages of vital government services were an “I told you so moment” highlighting Britain’s dependence on US tech.
